criteria.note: Structure + one-way: two events -> one epic (never forks), one child per work item keyed by the work item, routing target recorded; deep before/after compare proved plan_index unchanged; writes are seam epic/child ops only.
Routing enforced on the epic via the reused WARP-0601 tracker_for_repo (proven by spy, not reimplemented); no-tracker_repo, no-config, and unroutable plans skip by name and write nothing.

Burn-down rollup (mixed -> epic open, all-shipped -> epic shipped) and child statuses mapped through the same status_map; NG4 could not be broken (every set_status value is within status_map.values(); unmapped epic status annotated not transitioned; early-lifecycle child untouched).

Reconciler idempotency proven under replay, doubled event, out-of-order, replay-after-all-shipped, and reusing the same plan_index: no new transition, never forks an epic, state byte-identical. Reuses the WARP-0603 seam.

Non-tautology + teeth: a non-planning event builds no structure; mutation matrix turns the assertions red; build_plan_index is exercised over a real plan fixture and reverting its parser to front_matter turns 4 assertions red (childless-epic regression caught).

findings.text: Full independent adversarial review at fc722fb returned pass_with_notes, 0 blocking, confirming all 5 ACs by spies + a mutation matrix + an idempotency battery it could not break. It raised three notes: (1) SIGNIFICANT - build_plan_index used the shallow front_matter parser which collapses a plan's nested work DAG, so against real plans it returned zero work items (childless epics), and the read path had no test (green-but-hollow); (2) the one-way selftest reused an already-mirrored plan_index (dull teeth); (3) the W5/W6 child-status co-ownership deserved honest documentation.

All three notes were addressed in this commit (4d93272): build_plan_index now parses with parse_yamlish (the parser plan.py uses) and is covered by 5 selftest assertions over a REAL plan fixture (mutation-verified: reverting the parser turns 4 assertions red, and on the real repo the old code yields 0 work items for PLAN-0006 while the fix yields all 8 with live spec_status); the one-way guard now uses a fresh never-mirrored plan_index (mutation-verified: a stable-value writeback turns it red, whereas the old reused-index pattern stayed green); and the co-ownership is documented as a reconcile-to-truth (W6) + live-overlay (W5) design that converges at every persistent state, with only event-only statuses (in_review, merged) owned by the overlay between reconciles (stock configs leave them unmapped, so no flap). A scoped independent re-review bound to 4d93272 returned PASS with zero findings: the delta is exactly the three note-fixes, the five core functions (mirror_plan_events, _epic_warp_status, _child_identity, resolve_status_map, mirror_events) are byte-identical, the gate is GREEN (selftest 1157 passed, 0 failed) with the WARP-0605 spec-mirror block not regressed, and the two capabilities.yaml copies are byte-identical.

Operational: built in-session by a single writer (serialized single-writer discipline). No template twin ships for the mirror module (not a validate/policy_check load dependency), matching tracker_adapter.py and the spec mirror. The commit was verified GREEN in a clean detached worktree before and after the review fixes.

summary: W6 of PLAN-0006 (the plan-creates-structure epic mirror) is correct. Two independent adversarial reviews (a full pass on fc722fb, a scoped re-review bound to this shipped commit 4d93272) both PASS with 0 blocking. Planning-layer events drive a one-way projection of a plan's work DAG onto its tracker epic (keyed by the plan id, never forked, routing target recorded, per-repo routing enforced via the reused WARP-0601 resolver) and one child per work item (keyed by the work item), mirroring the burn-down (epic rollup + child statuses through the per-org status_map). It writes only epic/child status and fields, never a plan or spec, and never mutates its input plan index. It is a reconciler idempotent under at-least-once delivery with no offset ledger and no second store, reusing the WARP-0603 seam. A real defect in the repo-read bridge (build_plan_index using a parser that collapses the nested work DAG) was found by review and fixed with parse_yamlish + tested with teeth over a real plan fixture. Gate GREEN (selftest 1157 passed, 0 failed), no regression, no protected path. proof_digest via validate.py.
